text: Ever so often, we hear of bank account holders being flagged up and put through a lot of queries over the sources of funds in their own bank accounts while the real sharks swim away after gnawing an arm or a leg.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: In sum, we need a more proactive enforcement of our laws and licensing conditions.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: This has to be in addition to more effective oversight and not just closer monitoring of our financial institutions.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Notwithstanding the above, I am pleased that the Bill, in its provisions, for example, clause 174, expressly allows for the prosecution of directors and individuals involved in the management of the corporation for offences committed by corporations.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: This is a clear signal to fraudsters that there is no hiding behind the corporate veil.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: It is also broad enough to prosecute fraudsters who often avoid registering themselves as officers of corporations.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: I note that MAS does not intend to regulate non-fungible tokens (NFTs) for now.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: However, the NFT market is vulnerable to money laundering activities.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: In a recent study, the US Treasury Department revealed that NFTs may become a tool for money laundering in the high-value art market.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Recent sales of high-profile art pieces involving NFTs have sold for millions, indicating that this art sector has reached similar valuations as traditional art mediums.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: These art sectors using NFTs are popular vehicles for illicit financial flows.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: NFTs can even be used to conduct self-laundering.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: In this scenario, criminals may purchase a NFT with illicit funds and proceed to transact with themselves to create records of sales on the blockchain and wash the cash clean.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: I have asked several NFT-related Parliamentary Questions previously, given these concerns.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Member Derrick Goh had also spoken about this yesterday.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Can NFTs be brought into the definition of virtual assets so that the new rules will be applied equally to NFTs?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: I note the specification that the Bill covers VASPs created in Singapore or carrying on business of providing digital token services from a place of business in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: What about foreign digital token services which provide virtual assets activities within Singapore?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: I would also propose that we further streamline the capture of licensees under this Bill.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: MAS has explained that if a VASP is already licensed, exempted from licensing or required to be licensed under the relevant provisions in the Securities and Futures Act, Financial Advisers Act or Payment Services Acts, then it need not be licensed under the Financial Services and Markets Act (FSMA).

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Is it not possible to consolidate all of these licences under one omnibus Act?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: The technology sector progresses rapidly and funds flow in copious amounts daily.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: A 2018 International Monetary Fund (IMF) report stated that projected cyber attacks were costing financial institutions at least $100 billion globally on an annual basis.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: This figure would likely have risen with the sharp rise in technology progression and cybersecurity breaches in recent years.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: In this connection, financial institutions often have significant funds.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Also, inflation would degrade the deterrent effect of a fixed financial penalty.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: As such, how often will the range of financial penalties set out in the Bill be amended?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Singapore has built up a strong global reputation for reliability and resilience.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: This remains unwavering even in the face of recent global crises.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Swarths of capital and data from all over the world flow through our nation every day.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: We must continue to review our legislation on a regular basis to ensure that they remain robust and adequately comprehensive to support developments in our finance sector.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: In doing so, it empowers MAS to take a comprehensive sector-wide approach to risk management and enforcement action.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I have three points of clarification to raise.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: My first point is on the checks and balances against MAS' issuance of prohibition orders (POs).

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The Bill allows MAS to issue POs to persons based on MAS' fit and proper criteria.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: They restrict things as significant as shareholdings and as granular as business activity.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: They can end livelihoods and shut down companies.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Given the drastic nature of this enforcement action, it seems fair that MAS should, at least, explain the basis of such actions.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Clause 11 requires MAS to only give notice for and publish the PO.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: But it is entirely optional for MAS to explain its decision.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: In my view, MAS should be required to explain the rationale of its decision.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: It should, at least, state the category of fit and proper test criteria that the person has failed.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: To begin with, it seems only fair that we tell people why they are being punished.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: In addition, it would strengthen the mechanisms of accountability.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The Bill imposes two checks on MAS' issuance of POs.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: First, MAS is obligated to hear out the subject of the PO.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Second, the person can write an appeal to the Minister for Finance.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: In both cases, the process of justice would be strengthened if the person knows what he is being punished for.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: For example, if MAS explains that its PO is being issued due to a person's lack of financial soundness rather than due to dishonesty, that person could then present relevant evidence to the contrary.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: My second point is also about accountability in the issuance of POs.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Appeals are one key accountability mechanism for POs.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The Bill requires that the Minister considers the written report of the appeal advisory committee when deciding on these appeals.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: They can summon anyone to give evidence on oath and to produce any documents deemed necessary.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The committee's work thus affects not only the person issued the PO but also, potentially, a whole array of other people.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Given the extensive impact of the committee's work, it is not clear why their report should be shrouded in secrecy.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Publication of their written report would provide important context on the Minister's decision and ensure that these inquiries are held in a professional and appropriate way.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: My final point is on notices provided to financial institutions for POs issued and varied.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: MAS has stated that it will directly notify a person who is subject to the PO as well as the person's employer of the PO issued.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: In addition, how will MAS help ensure that financial institutions are notified in a timely manner when their service providers are issued a PO or have their PO varied?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: After all, financial institutions, typically, conduct due diligence checks on their service providers only at specific junctures.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Until they conduct such checks, they may not know that their service providers have been issued POs or have had their POs varied.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: It will be helpful to financial institutions if MAS can ensure PO issuances and variations are promptly communicated to financial institutions.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Members' comments and queries can be categorised into a few buckets and I will address them in turn.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Mr Don Wee, Mr Saktiandi Supaat, Mr Yip Hon Weng and Ms Janet Ang have raised questions on the scope of regulation of digital assets.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: MAS adopts a technology-neutral regulatory approach that focuses on the nature of the activity and the risks involved.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: VASPs, or what we term as digital token service providers in Singapore, DT service providers, are, therefore, regulated, based on the type of activity they conduct.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Correspondingly, where DT service providers deal in digital payment tokens, this could be a payment activity under the Payment Services Act.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Where they deal in or provide financial advice on capital market products, their activity would fall under the Securities and Futures Act (SFA) or the Financial Advisers Act (FAA).

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: These Acts are periodically reviewed to ensure that they remain fit-for-purpose and are in line with international norms.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: In most cases, DT service providers that incorporate or establish a place of business in Singapore do so to provide DT services in Singapore.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: They will be subject to the laws in Singapore.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Similarly, foreign DT service providers that provide DT services in Singapore will also be subject to the laws in Singapore.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Some of these businesses may also provide services in foreign markets and they would be expected to adhere to the rules that apply in the foreign markets where they operate.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: For instance, DT service providers that provide services in relation to capital market products in foreign countries would be subject to the rules imposed by the capital market regulators in the foreign countries concerned.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: MAS has cooperation arrangements with foreign regulators to ensure effective cross-border regulation.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: This approach is similar to the regulation of traditional capital market products that are not tokenised.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: It is, generally, not necessary to impose additional requirements on a business that is created and operating in Singapore if it does not provide services in Singapore.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: I would highlight that the FSM Bill also contains provisions that enable MAS to impose requirements across the financial sector to address money laundering and terrorism financing (ML/TF) risks.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Mr Saktiandi Supaat asked whether MAS has considered carving out DT service providers from licensing and regulation under the FSM Bill if they are already regulated in another jurisdiction which enforces the FATF standards.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Ms Janet Ang raised a similar question as well.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: There may be differences in the implementation and enforcement of these standards even as countries accept and adopt the enhanced FATF standards.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: DT service providers created in Singapore but providing their services outside of Singapore still pose reputational risks to Singapore.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Hence, regulating this group of DT service providers under the FSM Bill for ML/TF risks will mitigate these reputational risks.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Nonetheless, in response to comments made by Mr Saktiandi Supaat, Ms Janet Ang as well as Mr Louis Chua who had also asked about the scope of regulation, it is not the intention of MAS to subject a DT service provider who is regulated under another Act administered by MAS, to regulation under the FSM Bill, in respect of the same DT services.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Mr Saktiandi Supaat spoke also on the need to protect local consumers and markets from risks stemming from digital tokens, including those provided abroad, other than ML/TF risks.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Ms Janet Ang also raised concerns over the speculative nature of digital tokens and the need to educate the public.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: MAS has repeatedly warned the public on the risks of investing in digital tokens, such as digital payment tokens or cryptocurrencies, which would include the commonly known Bitcoin, for example.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: The prices of such digital payment tokens are not anchored on any economic fundamentals and are subject to sharp speculative swings.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Nonetheless, MAS is aware that there will continue to be people who choose to take these risks.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: MAS is monitoring the adoption of digital payment tokens in Singapore and will consider if user protection measures are needed.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: However, even with user protection measures, it is just not possible for laws to protect against investment losses, especially for consumers who choose to seek investment opportunities overseas or online.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Thus, consumer education and awareness remain key, as the best defence is a discerning public.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: MAS and relevant Government agencies have been and will continue to raise public awareness, including advising the public to not deal or invest with unregulated entities or investment products.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: They can continue, however, to promote their services on their own corporate website, mobile applications, or official social media accounts.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: However, they must not portray the trading in digital payment tokens in a manner that trivialises the associated risks.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: And this complements our continued consumer education efforts I mentioned earlier.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Mr Derrick Goh and Mr Yip Hon Weng asked if MAS will consider regulating non-fungible tokens (NFTs) given its rising popularity and its susceptibility as a vehicle for money laundering.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: NFTs, in its current form, are often digital representations of arts and other collectibles, which are not financial products subject to MAS regulation.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: As I have earlier mentioned, the FSM Bill will cover digital tokens that are either: one, a digital payment token; or two, a digital representation of a capital markets product.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: So, any digital token that meets the characteristics of a digital payment token or a capital market product could be subjected to regulation by MAS.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: All DT service providers must monitor transactions and file suspicious transaction reports with the Suspicious Transaction Reporting Office.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: The Cryptocurrency Task Force works closely with MAS and has links with the Association of Crypto Currency Enterprises and Start-ups Singapore (ACCESS), which is a Cryptocurrency and Blockchain Industry Association.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: SPF also works with the various cryptocurrency exchanges based locally and abroad to investigate cryptocurrency crimes.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: SPF takes a serious stance against any person who may be involved in cryptocurrency scams and crimes and perpetrators will be dealt with in accordance with the law.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Mr Louis Chua then also asked about the progress of licence applications for digital payment token (DPT) service providers under the PS Act.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: All applications go through a rigorous application process.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Applicants will know that MAS sets a high entry bar and commits time and resources to engage the applicants and scrutinise the applications, making sure that they are able to meet the required standards for managing ML/TF and technology risks before we approve their applications.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Applications that do not meet the standards or are incomplete will, naturally, need more time to review.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Mr Louis Chua also asked about the travel rule or the value transfer requirements in MAS' Notice PSN02 applicable to DPT service providers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: MAS will impose similar AML/CFT requirements to a DT service provider licensed under the FSM Bill.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Mr Louis Chua asked whether MAS would be inundated with transaction data, given the threshold of $1,500 to obtain certain information of the originator and beneficiary in a value transfer.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Contrary to Mr Louis Chua's understanding of the travel rule, there is actually no requirement for the originating DPT service providers to report this information to MAS.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Rather, they are required to relay the information to the beneficiary DPT service providers, for them to also conduct necessary screening for nefarious actors.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: The threshold of $1,500 is also aligned to the international standards for such cross-border transfers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Ms Janet Ang also asked if there is a regulatory gap, as financial advisory services related to digital payment tokens offered outside of Singapore will be regulated under the FSM Bill, but the same service offered in Singapore is not regulated under the PS Act.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: These financial advisory services are provided more often for capital market products and, in this respect, the FSM Bill places the same AML/CFT requirements on them as if they had been offered in Singapore.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: As for digital payment tokens, we will continue to study whether there is a meaningful presence of service providers that solely provide these advisory services.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Where entities provide these services along with other regulated services, such as dealing in, or facilitating the exchange of DPTs, they are already scoped into the PS Act.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: I will next move on to the second bucket which is questions that Members raised related to technology risk management (TRM).

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Mr Derrick Goh asked how MAS will weigh the accountability on FIs should negligence fall on the part of their cloud service providers, considering that many FIs have no ability to audit such providers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: MAS expects FIs to perform adequate due diligence on all third parties they engage.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: FIs remain responsible for any disruption that results from their service providers' negligence.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: And in determining the action to take against an FI, MAS will assess the impact of the breach, the extent to which necessary controls had been implemented to manage the outsourcing risk as well as to comply with MAS' requirements and remediation efforts.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Mr Yip Hon Weng asked how often the maximum penalty of $1 million per breach of a TRM requirement will be meted out for TRM lapses.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: He mentioned that, with inflation, a fixed financial penalty might not be a good deterrent.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: He also asked how often the financial penalties would be amended.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: In the event of a breach of TRM requirements, MAS will assess the breach to determine the appropriate course of action.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: In addition, MAS has the powers to take other supervisory actions, including requiring FIs to set aside additional regulatory capital until adequate measures have been put in place to address the control lapses or deficiencies.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: The financial penalty, coupled with the flexibility to impose additional supervisory actions, strikes a balanced approach which signals the importance of having robust TRM without being overly excessive for smaller FIs which Members have also asked about.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: As with other Acts which MAS administers, MAS will review and adjust the penalty framework under the FSM Bill, as necessary.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Mr Saktiandi Supaat suggested that MAS consider requiring prospective licensees to present adequate cybersecurity plans as a condition for granting licences.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Currently, when MAS assesses an application for a licence, MAS already considers factors, such as the adequacy of the applicant's cyber hygiene measures, data protection controls and the level of compliance with MAS' TRM guidelines.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Applicants that do not meet the requisite requirements will be rejected or given a conditional approval and such applicants will, eventually, still need to meet the requirements before they are allowed to offer their services.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Mr Saktiandi Supaat also referred to the PDPC's regulatory approach which considers the culpability of the offender when determining the appropriate enforcement actions.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: In accordance with MAS' current practice, MAS will take into account the nature of the breach of the TRM requirement, the specific circumstance of each case, the culpability of the offender and then calibrate supervisory action to ensure that they are appropriate and fair.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Assoc Prof Jamus Lim cited the rising trend of scams and the need for a consumer protection law to ensure that FIs do more to protect consumers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: The points he raised are not directly related to the Bill but I will briefly address them here.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: On the issue of combating scams, MAS, MCI and MHA have made three Ministerial Statements on 15 February this year to explain how the Government is undertaking a comprehensive approach to counter the threat of phishing scams.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: For the financial sector, Minister Lawrence Wong had elaborated at length on the measures by MAS and the banking industry, including measures that retail banks had implemented immediately and further measures which would be implemented to strengthen banks' ability to deter, detect and combat phishing scams.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Minister Lawrence Wong also highlighted that MAS was working with the industry to review the use of SMS to deliver one-time-passwords (OTPs) and also develop a loss-sharing framework to ensure an equitable sharing of losses for scams, based on the extent to which parties have fulfilled their responsibilities.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: For the sake of time, I will not repeat the points here.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: All banks offering PayNow are required to adhere to this.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Where a customer has installed and then activated a digital token in his or her mobile banking application, the digital token performs transaction signing in the background of the application, a process that is not obvious to the customer.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: MAS will reach out to Assoc Prof Jamus Lim to seek clarity on the facts relating to the PayNow experiment and the instance of the credit card limit being exceeded.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: On Assoc Prof Jamus Lim's points in support of a consolidated legislation to address consumer protection, let me clarify that there is no conflict between MAS' supervisory mandate and its role in consumer education and protection.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: MAS recognises that the core role of the financial sector is to serve the economy, businesses and consumers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: To do so, public confidence in financial services and FIs must be safeguarded.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: MAS sets out both prudential and business conduct standards for FIs, and expect them to operate safely and deal fairly with their customers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Both reinforce public confidence in FIs and the services that they provide.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: MAS has been able to effectively implement these standards and expectations through a mix of legislation, legally binding regulations and notices, as well as guidelines that are specific to the activities and risks in the different segments of the financial sector.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: This approach ensures that the requirements are relevant for the said regulated activities.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: For instance, banks are required to implement IT controls to protect customer information from unauthorised access and also the contravention of which can attract penalties.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Where consumers find themselves in a dispute with an FI that cannot be settled, MAS has provided consumers an avenue to seek recourse at a low-cost independent dispute resolution body – I mentioned yesterday in the FSM Bill – the Financial Industry Disputes Resolution Centre Ltd (FiDReC).

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Given these, there is no need to have a single consumer protection law for financial services.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: But I want to assure the Member that MAS continues to place a high priority on consumer education and protection.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: The functions that Assoc Prof Jamus Lim spoke of under the Market and Business Conduct Department continue to be taken up by the Market Conduct Policy and Consumer Issues Divisions.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: I will next move on to the prohibition order (PO) framework, of which we received many questions from Members.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Mr Derrick Goh asked how proximity will be assessed in determining whether a person has a nexus to the financial industry and whether staff from an FI’s service provider will be subject to a PO.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Proximity will be assessed in light of the policy objectives of this new PO powers, namely, to protect the financial industry, customers and investors against persons who have demonstrated, by their misconduct, that they have the potential to cause harm to, or are unsuitable to take up certain roles, activities and functions in the financial industry for which they are prohibited.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: In response to the example raised by Mr Derrick Goh, outsourced service providers who are individuals, such as those who work for IT vendors and ecosystem partners such as e-commerce platforms, may be subject to a PO.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: MAS recognises that outsourcing arrangements are becoming increasingly prevalent, but also complex, and MAS must be able to issue POs to service providers who have demonstrated by their misconduct that they have the potential to cause harm to the financial industry.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Whether a PO will be issued or not always depends on the specific circumstances of a case.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Mr Derrick Goh acknowledged that the basis for streamlining the disparate grounds for issuing POs under the SFA, FAA and Insurance Act into a single fit and proper test is sound – so, thank you for that.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: But he also sought clarification on whether there will be retrospective application of the single fit and proper test for persons with past misconduct that might not have been caught under the three Acts.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: If so, Mr Derrick Goh also asked whether the PO would commence from the point of misconduct.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: However, the single fit and proper test is not, in substance, a new test but rather, as Mr Derrick Goh acknowledges, streamlines the existing disparate grounds under the three Acts into one single test, based on MAS' guidelines on fit and proper criteria.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Thus, if a person's past misconduct would not have been caught under any of the three Acts, it is unlikely that MAS would assess that that person is not fit and proper under the new powers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: MAS will also continue to apply the old PO powers to cases where Notices of Intent to issue the prohibition order have already been given to the individual.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: A PO will not commence from the point of misconduct.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Mr Louis Ng asked why the Bill does not require MAS to publish an explanation for the imposition of POs, as it is only fair that people are being told why they are being punished.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: To clarify, before issuing any PO, MAS will always issue a Notice of Intention to a person informing them that MAS intends to issue a PO against him or her.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: This Notice of Intention will set out all the material facts and grounds on which MAS has determined that a person is not fit and proper.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: There is, hence, no unfairness as the person will be fully aware of the basis for which MAS intends to issue a PO against him or her.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: In any case, the person is given the opportunity to respond by sending representations to MAS.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: MAS will carefully consider such representations before making its decision whether to issue a PO against the person.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Mr Saktiandi Suppat asked if an individual's previous PO can be purged from the records after a specific period of time.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Therefore, where POs are of a shorter duration, the information on the PO will remain on the webpage for a period of five years from the date of publication.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Where the PO is longer than five years, the information on the PO will be removed when the PO expires.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Effectively, this means that information on POs will not remain on MAS' "Enforcement Actions" webpage forever and will be removed from the webpage after five years for POs with a duration shorter than five years, or after the PO expires, where the PO is longer than five years.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: The minimum duration for enforcement actions to remain on the "Enforcement Actions" webpage is, therefore, five years.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: And the duration is fair, because it takes into account: one, the need to send a deterrent message to others that the misconduct justifying the enforcement action – for example, for breaching MAS-administered laws – is a grave matter; and two, the period of five years is also broadly consistent with the period after which a conviction for an eligible crime could also be spent under the Registration of Criminals Act.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Mr Yip Hon Weng asked if a person has been placed on a watchlist or issued something of equivalence to our PO by an overseas jurisdiction, would they be issued a PO here by default.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: While this is a factor that MAS will consider in applying the fit and proper test, MAS will consider all the circumstances of the case, including the facts surrounding why such a person has been placed on a watchlist or the equivalent of a PO, before deciding whether to issue a PO.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Mr Yip Hon Weng also mentioned that a person issued with a PO may be prohibited from becoming a substantial shareholder of an FI.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: In this context, he also asked whether it will be an offence to wilfully assist the PO individual to evade the PO.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: The answer is: this could amount to an offence.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: And to be clear, it is an offence for a person who has been issued a PO to contravene the PO.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: If a third party assists this person to contravene the PO, then the third party could also be liable for abetting the commission of the offence.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Mr Louis Ng has sought clarification on whether MAS will notify the individual's employer if his PO is varied and how MAS will help to ensure that FIs are notified in a timely manner if their service providers are issued a PO, or have their PO varied.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: MAS will send out these notifications concurrently with the issuance of a PO or a varied PO.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: This is to ensure that the individual's employer is informed in a timely manner.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: MAS will consider whether and how to notify FIs if their service providers have been issued a PO or have their POs varied.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Mr Derrick Goh asked if existing and incoming foreign talent will be subject to the same due diligence as that of local staff and, if so, whether clearer guidelines on the background checks for foreign talent would be issued.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: This is because misconduct in non-regulated but critical functions may not be captured in overseas registries.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Insofar as POs are concerned, the "due diligence" and "background checks" that would have to be conducted by an FI, whether under the current framework or the new framework, is to ensure that they do not hire individuals who have been issued a PO by MAS to perform the roles or activities that have been prohibited.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: This applies to both foreign and local employees.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: FIs can check the MAS' "Enforcement Actions" webpage or write to MAS to enquire whether a particular individual has been issued a PO by MAS.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Mr Derrick Goh also mentioned that the Bill has broadened the scope for MAS to issue POs covering activities beyond MAS-administered Acts, including serious misconduct in activities, such as fund management, risk and technology management, which were previously not covered.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: To this end, Mr Derrick Goh has also asked what the severity thresholds for misconduct are, how proportionality of prohibitions is assessed and how culpability for misconduct would be assessed across the ranks, from junior staff to senior management.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: To clarify, while the Bill does broaden the scope for MAS to issue POs, handling of funds, risk management and administration of critical systems are areas that have an important impact on the soundness and integrity of our financial sector and MAS does exercise regulatory oversight over such areas.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: MAS has set standards of practice for these functions through the issuance of regulations, notices and guidelines.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: On how proportionality of the prohibition is assessed, if Mr Derrick Goh is asking how the duration and scope of a PO is determined, one can expect that the more serious the misconduct is, the longer the duration and wider the scope of the PO are likely to be.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Ultimately, each case will be assessed on its own merits, its own facts, taking into account factors that I mentioned previously.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: To respond to Mr Saktiandi Supaat's question on whether an FI would be able to "shift" the regulatory burden to its service providers when employing the defence to show that it had taken all reasonable steps to ensure compliance that it has not employed, directly or indirectly, or used the services of a person against whom a PO has been made, there will be no "shift" in the regulatory burden as FIs are still, ultimately, responsible for checking that their service providers' relevant employees, who directly or indirectly undertake key functions for or on behalf of the FIs, have not been issued with POs prohibiting them to do so.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: For an FI to avail itself of the defence, the FI must, minimally, show that they have performed due diligence checks on the employees of its service providers, for example, again, checking the MAS' "Enforcement Actions" webpage.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Mr Yip Hon Weng also shared that it is not difficult for seasoned fraudsters to set up businesses here and cheat customers, which calls for a more proactive enforcement of our laws.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: This is in line with what the PO powers are trying to achieve, by pre-emptively and comprehensively keeping known bad actors out of our financial industry.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: For now, the search function on the "Enforcement Actions" webpage may be used by any FI or its agent, to check if a PO is currently in effect against a person.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Alternatively, there is also an option for the FI or its agent to contact MAS to obtain records of the POs issued against the person, upon payment of a fee.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: There is, hence, sufficient means for an FI to determine if an individual has been issued with a PO.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Mr Saktiandi Supaat then spoke on the need for clarity in the form of MAS guidance on the specific scope of POs issued in the newly-extended areas.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: He also asked for data on the number of persons who had previously been issued with a PO and who have thereafter returned to the financial sector.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Clauses 6 and 7 of the Bill sets out clearly the scope of POs which may be issued, which are to prohibit unsuitable persons from certain roles, activities and functions.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: There is no ambiguity here on the maximum possible scope of a PO.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: In summary, the more serious the misconduct is, the longer the duration, the wider the scope of the PO is likely to be.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: MAS does not monitor whether persons who have previously been issued with a PO return to the financial sector after the PO expires.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: To be clear, a PO only bars an individual from taking up specified roles, functions and activities in the financial industry.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: An individual is free to take up employment in the financial industry in areas or activities that are not covered by the PO or even outside the financial industry.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: An individual may choose to find employment in the areas prohibited by the PO when the PO expires.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: And in such a scenario, it is then up to their prospective employers to determine independently whether or not to hire such a person.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Mr Derrick Goh has noted that an appeal to the Minister on MAS' decision to issue a PO must be referred to an Appeal Advisory Committee selected from an Appeal Advisory Panel (AAP).

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: He asked about the considerations for ensuring the independence of the AAP and Committee.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: He also asked whether, in addition to the right of appeal to the Minister, a person may bring his appeal to the Court.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: On the first question, the members of the AAP will be appointed by the Minister from the financial industry and the public and private sectors, and will have strong credentials which attest to their good judgment and ability to discharge their duties professionally.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: The AAC will comprise any three members from this panel.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Under the existing regulations governing appeals to the Minister for PO purposes, the AAC is obliged to declare the nature and extent of all of their conflicts of interest or potential conflicts of interest to the Minister.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: If the Minister is satisfied that any AAC member is unable to discharge his duties effectively because of any conflict of interest or potential conflict of interest, the Minister may replace the AAC member.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: This will also be the process in appeals to the Minister under the new Act.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: On the second question, a person will be afforded the right to appeal to the Minister under the new Act.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: This avenue of appeal under the new Act is consistent with the existing practice under the SFA, FAA and IA.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: However, if a person has exhausted his right of appeal to the Minister and remains unsatisfied with the results, he may still pursue other legal processes which he may be entitled to.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Mr Louis Ng asked why the AAC's reports are not published publicly.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: He suggests that, first, this would provide important context on the Minister's decision and, secondly, ensure that the AAC exercises its powers professionally and appropriately.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: On the first aspect, the Minister is not bound by the recommendations in the AAC's report but, rather, exercises his own discretion in deciding on the appeal.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: The Minister may agree with some of the AAC's assessments while disagreeing with other aspects.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: He may consider other factors outside the AAC's report.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Thus, publishing the AAC's report may not be all that helpful and may even be an inaccurate reflection of the Minister's considerations.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: On the second aspect, as mentioned in response to a previous question by Mr Derrick Goh, the members of the AAP, from which the AAC is constituted, will be appointed by the Minister and will have strong credentials which will attest to their good judgement and ability.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: If the AAC in any way exercises its powers improperly, the parties can always include this in their submissions, which the Minister will consider.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Mr Saktiandi Supaat also asked when the new PO regime under the FSM Bill will be brought into effect.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: This is a matter which MAS is considering carefully.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: MAS is, currently, preparing for the new PO regime to commence and also intends to give the industry time to prepare for the new PO regime, which includes understanding how the new provisions will be applied.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: It is on the provision of statutory protection for personnel of the operator of an approved dispute resolution scheme.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Mr Yip Hon Weng asked if there will be exceptions to this.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: For statutory protection to be accorded, the mediator, adjudicator or employee must have acted with reasonable care and in good faith.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: This will have to be determined, based on the facts and circumstances of each case.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Ms Janet Ang asked broadly about MAS' plans to enhance the skills and competencies required in the financial services ecosystem.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: MAS works closely with the industry, such as the Institute of Banking and Finance, to develop the workforce in the financial sector.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: To seize opportunities for growth, we are always on the lookout for new growth drivers, including from the digitalisation wave.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: To meet the new job demands, we also have multiple training pathways to reskill and upskill our financial sector talent.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Ms Janet Ang and Mr Louis Chua asked broadly about central bank digital currencies (CBDCs).

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Minister of State, may I ask if you will be going on further?

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: You have one and a half minutes left.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: If you can wrap up within one and a half minutes, then I will not ask the Leader to extend.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Yes, I will wrap up within one and a half minutes.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: The details and conclusions of the project, you can find on the BIS website.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: So, you can find them on our website.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: MAS regularly reviews its Acts to ensure —

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Just on the safe side, let us extend.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: It is a chunky Bill; I am almost at the end.
